memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not defraud or rob your neighbour. Do not hold back the wages of a hired worker overnight.'" - Lev 19:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Do not hold back the wages of a hired worker overnight. This is one of those verses that reveals how closely God pays attention.

A day labourer in Israel had no savings. He worked, he was paid, and that money bought his family's food that evening. Delay his wages by a single night, and his children went hungry.

The employer might not even notice. He would settle up tomorrow, or at the end of the week — a small administrative convenience. But God says no. Not overnight. Because what is a minor delay to the person with money is a crisis for the person without it.

That is the heart of this law. God sees the gap between inconvenience for the powerful and disaster for the vulnerable, and He legislates on behalf of the one with less.

James picks this up with real force, writing to wealthy landowners: the wages you failed to pay the workers who mowed your fields are crying out against you (Jas 5:4). The unpaid wages themselves cry out, and God hears.

Most of us are not employers. But the principle reaches wider. Do you pay people promptly? Do you keep someone waiting because the delay costs you nothing? Do you settle up with the person who cannot chase you?

God notices what we consider too small to matter.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there someone you owe money, time, or thanks who is still waiting?
2. Where does your convenience cost someone else more than you realise?
3. How can you be prompt and fair in your dealings this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You notice what I think is too small to matter. Make me prompt and fair, especially with people who have no power to chase me. Amen.
